children: Wall Street ended the week lower, with investors digesting a sharp rise in Treasury yields and the latest inflation data.
The benchmark 10-year yield climbed nearly 20 bps to 4.97%, while CPI rose 0.4% M/M in August, in line with estimates and up from July’s 0.1% gain.
For the week, the blue-chip Dow
fell -1.57%, the benchmark S&P (
) lost -0.80%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite
handed back -0.66%.
Here's what caught investor attention this week:
Apple
formally unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, at its Sept. 9 product event. The Duo has a foldable display and starts at $1,999, with availability scheduled for Oct. 23.
Novartis
shares fell about 14% on Tuesday after the company reported that del-desiran, an experimental drug designed to fight muscle-wasting disease, failed to meet the primary endpoint in a late-stage trial.
Meta

officially introduced Muse as a personal AI agent designed to proactively help users accomplish goals and handle tasks. It can, with user authorization, do things such as send emails, book travel, shop, make payments, and manage other digital tasks.
Oracle

shares jumped after the IT giant reported fiscal first-quarter results and guidance that beat Wall Street estimates. Revenue rose 30% year over year, while cloud revenue climbed 62% to $11.6B, driven largely by a 121% surge in infrastructure revenue.
Quantum computing stocks
, Rigetti Computing
, Quantum Computing
, and Quantinuum

, rallied on Tuesday following a combined $300M CHIPS Act funding commitment from the U.S. Department of Commerce. Rigetti will target hardware scaling bottlenecks and cryostat architectures, D-Wave will scale annealing and gate-model technology, and Quantinuum will partner with GlobalFoundries on ion trap manufacturing. In exchange for the funding, the government will receive minority equity stakes in Rigetti and D-Wave.
Adobe

shares fell even as the Photoshop maker reported second-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's estimates. Q2 adjusted were $6.13 per share, while revenue rose 13% year-over-year to $6.76B. For the full year, Adobe now expects to earn between $24.45 and $24.50 per share on an adjusted basis, up from a previous range of $24.35 to $24.45 per share.
Skyworks Solutions

rose almost 9% on Friday, pushing the stock above its 52-week high as the analog semiconductor maker continued a strong multi-session run. The move followed an almost 10% gain in the previous session, extending what has become a sustained upswing since early September. SWKS advanced nearly 19% over the week.
CooperCompanies

fell after issuing fiscal third quarter results that included guidance revisions below the consensus. FY 2026 revenue guidance of $4.229B-$4.252B (from $4.285B-$4.321B prior) is below the consensus of $4.31B. Non-GAAP diluted EPS is seen at $4.51-$4.55 ($4.58-$4.66 prior), which is below the consensus of $4.63.
Macy's

reported a stronger-than-expected second quarter, with comparable sales up 2.7%, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of comparable-sales growth. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 41.5% during the quarter, with nearly all of that increase reflected in tariff refunds. Adjusted EPS rose to $0.63 from $0.35 a year earlier and topped the consensus estimate of $0.37.
Intel

shares rose on Tuesday after Northland Securities upgraded the semiconductor giant and a report emerged about potential price hikes. Northland analyst Gus Richard raised his rating to Outperform from Market Perform and said the company has made “material progress” in its turnaround. He also noted Intel is likely to keep benefiting from the ongoing server CPU shortage. Separately, Digitimes reported that Intel is set to raise prices on its CPUs by as much as 10%, citing multiple sources familiar with the matter.

title: Trending stocks this week as markets end lower amid inflation, yield jitters
